schema_note: Seed list for C6/C1 (Versed Parallel rights inventory + benchmark v0.1 pre-aligned sources). All source_url values are URLs actually observed in WebSearch results during compilation on 2026-08-12 -- none constructed from memory. pd_rationale is a rationale, not a legal opinion; D6b (EU/French IP counsel) still gates any commercial use per the roadmap. Uncertain items are marked confidence:'low' rather than asserted as safe.
compiled_for: VERSED_TRANSLATION_ROADMAP.md C6 checkpoint 1 / C7 gold-work candidates

entries.work_english_title: The Origins of the Islamic State
entries.author: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Baladhuri (d. 892)
entries.translator: Philip K. Hitti (vol. 1); Francis Clark Murgotten (vol. 2)
entries.translator_death_year: Hitti d. 1978 (PD rests on publication date, not translator death, for this entry)
entries.digital_form: both (page scans + OCR/djvu text)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1916/1924, both well before the 1930 US pre-1930-publication PD cutoff; Columbia University Press edition, no renewal found in search pass.

Also digitized separately at https://archive.org/details/originsislamics00hittgoog and full text at https://archive.org/stream/originsislamics00hittgoog/originsislamics00hittgoog_djvu.txt (both URLs seen in search results). Strong C7 gold-work candidate.

Additional volumes at https://archive.org/details/32882019293979-ibnkhallikansbi (v.4) and https://archive.org/details/32882019293961-ibnkhallikansbi (v.3), both seen in search results. entries.work_arabic_title: Muruj al-Dhahab wa-Ma'adin al-Jawhar (مروج الذهب ومعادن الجوهر)

Useful for partial alignment / QE test material only, not a full-book C7 gold candidate as-is.

entries.work_english_title: Kalila and Dimna, or The Fables of Bidpai
entries.author: Abdullah Ibn al-Muqaffa' (d. c. 757), after the Sanskrit/Pahlavi tradition

entries.notes: Complete translation, directly from Arabic (not a derivative branch). Strong C7 gold-work candidate alongside Baladhuri/Ibn Khallikan/Hariri -- shortlisted as a close 4th.

entries.pd_rationale: Published 1885, translator died 1887; comfortably PD.
entries.notes: Translated from the later Syriac recension, NOT directly from the Arabic Ibn al-Muqaffa' text -- flagged so it is not mistakenly used as a direct Arabic-English aligned pair without checking which recension it actually reflects.

entries.work_arabic_title: Rihlat Ibn Battuta (تحفة النظار في غرائب الأمصار وعجائب الأسفار)
entries.work_english_title: The Travels of Ibn Batuta
entries.author: Ibn Battuta (d. 1368/69)
entries.digital_form: both (scan + full text at https://archive.org/stream/b28406084/b28406084_djvu.txt, seen in search results)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1829 (Oriental Translation Fund); translator died 1852. Comfortably PD.
entries.notes: IMPORTANT: Lee translated only the ABRIDGED Arabic manuscript copies held in the Cambridge Public Library, not the full Rihla. The complete/critical translation is H.A.R. Gibb's Hakluyt Society edition (1958-2000, Gibb d. 1971) -- that one is NOT public domain and must not be used.

entries.work_english_title: The Assemblies of Al-Hariri
entries.author: Abu Muhammad al-Qasim ibn Ali al-Hariri (d. 1122)
entries.digital_form: both (full text stream + associated scans on archive.org)
entries.pd_rationale: Both volumes published pre-1900; both translators died before 1930. Comfortably PD by either rule.
entries.notes: Together the two volumes form a COMPLETE translation of all 50 assemblies (Oriental Translation Fund New Series). Strong C7 gold-work candidate.

entries.work_english_title: The History of Hayy Ibn Yaqzan (originally: The Improvement of Human Reason)
entries.author: Abu Bakr Muhammad Ibn Tufayl (d. 1185)
entries.digital_form: both (scan + OCR text)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1708/1731; translator died 1720. Unambiguously PD.
entries.notes: Use the original 1708/1731 Ockley text, NOT the 1929 A.S. Fulton-revised edition (revision introduces a possible fresh copyright layer and its editor's death year was not confirmed in this pass). A 1929-revision copy exists at https://archive.org/details/IbnTufailStoryOfHayyBinYaqzanHistoryOckleyIntroFulton -- flagged, not selected as the primary source. Do not fetch Gutenberg 34572 (Brönnle Wisdom of the East abridgement).

entries.work_arabic_title: Kimiya-yi Sa'adat (كيمياى سعادت) -- Persian condensation related to the Arabic Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din
entries.work_english_title: The Alchemy of Happiness
entries.author: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (d. 1111)
entries.digital_form: both (scan + text; also on Wikisource at https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/The_Alchemy_of_Happiness_(Field), seen in search results)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1910; translator died 1941 (>70y as of 2026, since 1941+70=2011). PD by both rules.
entries.notes: CAVEAT: the original is in Persian (Ghazali's own condensation of his Arabic Ihya'), and some sourcing indicates Field translated from an intermediate Hindustani/Urdu version rather than directly from Persian -- a multi-step translation chain. Genre-relevant but not a clean direct Arabic-English pair; flagged for QE/register analysis use rather than as a C7 alignment gold work in its current form. OpenITI URI mapped to Kimiya-yi Sa'adat, but note OpenITI's Arabic-corpus focus may treat this as a distinct (Persian) work from the Arabic Ihya'.

entries.work_arabic_title: (anthology of multiple pre-Islamic and early-Islamic poets)

entries.notes: Anthology, not one OpenITI work. Verse OCR is poor. File: lyall_arabian_poetry_2015.50391_djvu.txt. Do not map as 1885.

entries.work_arabic_title: Sirat 'Antar ibn Shaddad (سيرة عنترة بن شداد)

entries.notes: Hamilton translated only part of the very long Sirat Antar cycle (4 vols covering the opening portion) -- NOT a complete translation of the whole romance. Good for a bounded excerpt alignment task, not a full-book C7 candidate.

entries.work_arabic_title: (Lane's own notes/study drawn from Alf Layla wa-Layla, ألف ليلة وليلة)

entries.translator: Edward William Lane (ed. Stanley Lane-Poole, posthumous)
entries.digital_form: both (scan + text; also Project Gutenberg https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/41110 marked PD-in-USA, seen in search results)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1883 (posthumous); translator/author died 1876. Comfortably PD.
entries.genre: adab / social history (secondary study, not a direct work-translation)
entries.notes: FLAG: this is Lane's compiled explanatory notes and essays drawn FROM his 1001 Nights translation, not itself a straight translation of a single Arabic work -- included for genre diversity and background/QE-register use, but should not be treated as a C7 alignment gold-work pair without care.

entries.work_english_title: Mishkat-ul-Masabih (a collection of the most authentic traditions)
entries.author: Wali al-Din al-Khatib al-Tabrizi (compiler, d. c. 1340s), based on al-Baghawi's Masabih al-Sunna
entries.digital_form: both (scan + text, per search results)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1809-1810, over two centuries ago; comfortably PD by publication date.
entries.notes: Earliest known printed English translation of Mishkat al-Masabih. Per roadmap D6c: this is an independent 1809 PD text, NOT hadith-json/Sunnah.com material, so the standing 'index-only, never ships' constraint on Sunnah.com content does not automatically apply here -- but flag for a human rights check before use, since the digitized copy circulating online may be a later (post-1930) re-edited/annotated reprint (the F. K. Khan Durrani revision) rather than the bare 1809 text; confirm which edition the archive.org text actually is before use.

entries.work_arabic_title: Sirat Rasul Allah (سيرة رسول الله), Ibn Hisham's recension of Ibn Ishaq
entries.work_english_title: The Life of Muhammad (a translation of Ibn Ishaq's Sirat Rasul Allah)
entries.author: Muhammad Ibn Ishaq (d. c. 767), via Ibn Hisham's recension (d. 833)
entries.publication_year: translated before 1891; manuscript presented to the Royal Asiatic Society 1898; publication/print history unclear
entries.digital_form: text (djvu/full text stream; scan status not confirmed)
entries.pd_rationale: Translator died 1891 (>70y ago), which favors PD, but the actual first-publication date and edition lineage is murky -- some sources describe only an abridged 1964 Folio Society/Michael Edwardes edition as the first PRINTED form, which would carry its own (non-PD) editorial layer.
entries.notes: Do NOT confuse with A. Guillaume's 1955 translation of the same underlying work (Guillaume d. 1965, published 1955 -- NOT public domain, must be excluded). The archive.org text found here claims to be Rehatsek's rendering but its provenance/edition needs verification before any use; treat as a lead, not a confirmed source.

entries.work_english_title: The Qur'an (Sacred Books of the East, vols. VI and IX)
entries.author: (scripture)
entries.digital_form: both (scan + text; series entry also at https://archive.org/details/1922707.0014.002.umich.edu, seen in search results)
entries.pd_rationale: Published 1880 (Oxford, Sacred Books of the East series ed. F. Max Muller); translator died 1882. Unambiguously PD.
entries.notes: Included for genre completeness/diversity even though the Qur'an sits outside the 'classical Arabic literary works' framing of most of this list; useful given how central Qur'anic-quotation matching is to the C7 alignment pipeline (structural anchors) and C5 fidelity checks.

entries.notes: Only a HathiTrust catalog record was directly observed, not a confirmed full-view/downloadable text -- Archive.org and Gutenberg copies were referenced by secondary sources (booksellers, an Archive.org 'Wilfrid Scawen Blunt' biography stream) but no exact full-text URL for THIS specific 1903 edition was confirmed in this pass. OpenITI URI guess is approximate: mapped to the closest priority-list entry (al-Zawzani's classical commentary on the Mu'allaqat), not a raw diwan of the seven odes -- needs a human check against the actual poem texts before use.

Gorgias 2002 is a facsimile with a new copyright on special contents. Do not fetch either.

entries.translator_death_year: Hitti d. 1978 (US PD is the 1929 publication year, not translator death)
entries.digital_form: both (scan + OCR)
entries.pd_rationale: 1929 US publication. Under the US 95-year term this entered the US public domain on 1 January 2025. Not PD_US_PRE_1930 (that cutoff is 1928). Not a claim about EU life+70 (Hitti d. 1978). Jurisdiction: US (Bilal, 2026-08-16, US citizen).
entries.notes: Use the 1929 scan only. Drop 1964 / 1987 / 2000 reprints. Benchmark genre-cap (history/memoir) is a separate factory decision from this rights stamp.

entries.work_english_title: The Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night (Payne)
entries.author: Anonymous
entries.digital_form: both (multi-volume scans + OCR)
entries.pd_rationale: Payne 1882-84. US PD by 19th-century publication. Jurisdiction: US (Bilal, 2026-08-16). Prefer Payne over Burton (Burton's archaism is a poor MT reference).
entries.notes: One public edition (Payne), not 487 catalog rows. Prefer Gutenberg 8655-8658 (vols I-IV, clean) then UofT IA arabiannights05-09paynuoft (vols V-IX, 1901 subscribers). Burton 3435-3444 and Mathers/Mardrus stay catalog-only. Confirm which Arabic recension OpenITI has before aligning.

entries.work_english_title: The Koran (Al-Qur'an), translated by J. M. Rodwell
entries.author: (scripture)
entries.publication_year: 1861 (this Gutenberg text is the later reprint with Margoliouth introduction)
entries.digital_form: Gutenberg proofread text
entries.pd_rationale: First published 1861; translator died 1900. Gutenberg 3434 is US PD. Cleaner than Palmer OCR. Print order is chronological, not canonical — align by the canonical sura number in each heading (SURA LXXIV etc.), not by file order.
entries.notes: 109 SURA headers verified. Do not pair consecutive Gutenberg paragraphs to consecutive OpenITI suras. Palmer 1880 remains the canonical-order PD Quran already on disk. Pickthall 1930 is US PD as of 1 Jan 2026 but Wikisource export is bot-walled.

entries.work_english_title: The Koran, commonly called the Alkoran of Mohammed, translated by George Sale
entries.author: (scripture)
entries.digital_form: Gutenberg proofread text
